knowledge_point.title: Rewriting a Triple Integral Defined Over a Cylindrical Solid

question.:question/problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the cylinder ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=27$ between the surfaces $z=0$ and $z=11-x.$
Express the following triple integral in cylindrical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}z\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the formulas

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

First, let's sketch the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/edb-math/repairs/2026-10-28-topic-audit-3/published-probe/17592186129267/17592186129267/projection-4f127f8a9564b4a4510b6ff1722da20127ce79410c97a383cec5697934d2b6d7.png)

The region $R$ is a right vertical cylinder of radius $3 \sqrt{3}$ whose axis passes through the point $(0,0)$ in the $xy$-plane, and is

- bounded below by $z=0,$ and

- bounded above by $z=11-x=11-r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta ,z)\,:\,0\le r\le 3 \sqrt{3},\,0\le \theta <2\pi ,\,0\le z\le 11-r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}z\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}z\sqrt{(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}}\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}z\sqrt{{r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )}\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{3 \sqrt{3}}{\int }_{0}^{11-r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{r}^{2}z\,dz\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$
